races.title: State Assembly, District 38
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Steve Bennett
cands.bio: Democratic incumbent in the California State Assembly (District 38, western Ventura County), first elected in 2020. A former high school economics and American history teacher, he served on the Ventura City Council (1993–1997) and the Ventura County Board of Supervisors (2000–2020).

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia: Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions AFL-CIO, California Nurses Association, California Teachers Association, National Union of Healthcare Workers, California Environmental Voters, Equality California, and others.

His campaign site lists California Professional Firefighters, United Farm Workers, SEIU, Planned Parenthood Central Coast Action Fund, Sen. Alex Padilla, Rep. Julia Brownley, Rep. Salud Carbajal and Senate President pro Tem Monique Limón, among others.

cands.gaps: We couldn't find the year Bennett moved to California or details of his upbringing beyond "the Midwest." We found no documented positions or actions on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, school choice, or teacher pay. We found no record of his stance on red-flag laws or other gun legislation beyond a campaign-site label. We found no documented controversies or foreign ties. The pages we had were not detailed on his Assembly-era actions, other than a 2024 octopus-farming ban he authored. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in any year.

local.label: Roots 55: He was born in Indianapolis and raised in the Midwest, and the record shows him living in Ventura by 1991 (a write-in council run) and serving there continuously since, which is 25+ years as an adult resident.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assemblymember since 2020; Ventura County Supervisor 2000–2020, including several terms as board chair; Ventura City Councilmember 1993–1997; high school teacher for about 20 years, later a counseling department head and assistant principal.
qual.why: He has about five years of state legislative service plus two decades as a county supervisor and a city council term, all of which involve writing law and setting budgets. His campaign site says he brought fiscal discipline and balanced budgets to the county.
qual.label: He has about five years of state legislative service plus two decades as a county supervisor and a city council term, all of which involve writing law and setting budgets. His campaign site says he brought fiscal discipline and balanced budgets to the county.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: In the 1990s he was spokesman for Voters for Alternate Sites, which opposed building a new California State University campus near the Robert Taylor Ranch in Ventura.

back-police-order.evidence: During a city budget discussion (undated in the source) he said "no way would I support cutting the police budget" and that he was comfortable cutting $100,000 from other areas.

workers-first.evidence: As a Ventura city councilmember in 1994 he voted for a resolution opposing Proposition 187, which would have restricted illegal immigrants' access to healthcare and education.

second-amendment.evidence: His campaign site lists him as a 2026 Moms Demand Action "Gun Sense Candidate" and notes this is a designation, not an endorsement by Moms Demand Action or Everytown.

clean-money.evidence: On the Ventura City Council he pushed a $100 campaign contribution limit; the council voted it down 4–2, then voted 5–2 to put it on the ballot as Measure H, which voters passed. He had refused donations above $100 in his own council campaign.

pro-life.evidence: In 1995 he voted on the Ventura City Council (4–3) to have the city attorney file a brief supporting Santa Barbara's appeal of a ruling that struck down an eight-foot bubble ordinance outside family planning clinics.

prio.label: Matches 3 of 6 priorities; 4 backed by their record, 1 only promised

roots.summary: He was born in Indianapolis and raised in the Midwest, and the record shows him living in Ventura by 1991 (a write-in council run) and serving there continuously since, which is 25+ years as an adult resident.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: His campaign site says he protected Ventura County's open spaces and agricultural land from massive LA urban sprawl projects through a series of land use initiatives (SOAR).

cands.name: Michael MacDonald
cands.bio: Ventura City Clerk, overseeing elections, public records and legislative processes. Previously Assistant City Clerk in Berkeley and Port Hueneme, and staff to state Senators Fran Pavley, Hannah-Beth Jackson and Scott Wiener. Former Chair of the Oakland Public Ethics Commission. Democrat who ran for Assembly District 38.

endorsements.text: Listed on Ballotpedia as recommended in three voter guides: April's Common Sense Cali Voters, Based in Malibu, and Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide. Ballotpedia notes his own survey said endorsements were still forming.

cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace or the year he returned to Ventura County as an adult. We found no record of any elected office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. He has no documented stance on homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign buyers of homes and land, gun laws, abortion, school choice or teacher pay, or on refusing donations from particular groups. On data centers, his site says only that he will push for responsible growth protecting water and energy as AI and data centers expand, which is not a clear position for or against, so we left it out. Nothing we read shows how he would handle statewide budget or tax questions.

local.label: Roots 90: His campaign site says he attended Pierpont Elementary in Ventura County, spent summers there growing up and later returned to build his life and career there, and he told Ballotpedia he grew up in Ventura County; his birthplace is not stated.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Ventura City Clerk; earlier Assistant City Clerk for Berkeley and Port Hueneme; Office Manager to Sen. Fran Pavley and District Representative to Sens. Hannah-Beth Jackson and Scott Wiener; Senior Advisor to Regional Government Services; Chair of the Oakland Public Ethics Commission.
qual.why: He has years of legislative staff and municipal government management experience, including work on legislative processes and policy. He has held no elected office and no legislative budget-writing role, so he lands in the middle band; the ethics commission chair seat adds nothing to the score.

workers-first.evidence: Says he will oppose indiscriminate immigration enforcement, defend due process for immigrant communities and support pathways for immigrants to work and build businesses.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Says he will dramatically expand housing supply at every level, accelerate permitting, lower building costs and reward jurisdictions that deliver housing results.

back-police-order.evidence: Says in his Ballotpedia survey that he will support law enforcement and well-resourced first responders, alongside prevention, mental health co-response teams and a homelessness approach balancing compassion with accountability.
